title: On-Prem Inference: Sales Playbook & Comparative Notes
content:
Purpose
This is a lightweight field playbook for conversations where buyers are evaluating in-house inference stacks (vLLM, TGI, TensorRT-LLM, FasterTransformers, Ollama, etc.) vs. purchasing Redwood’s hosted/dedicated/private inference. Goal: give AE/SEs quick talking points, cost/risk heuristics, rebuttals to common objections, and a proposed POC path that highlights Redwood's differentiated risk reduction and operational economics.

Audience
- Enterprise ML/platform leads contemplating self-hosting for cost, control, or compliance reasons.
- Platform engineering teams evaluating a roadmap to move inference from R&D -> prod.

High-level positioning (elevator lines)
- "If you want to own every layer of your inference stack and have the time and people to run it, vLLM/TGI/TensorRT variants are great. If you want predictable latency, SLA-backed uptime, and the tooling to operate ML at scale without hiring a large infra team, Redwood gets you production-grade serving in weeks not quarters."
- Quick alternative: "Build when the business differentiator is the model itself and you need complete bespoke kernels. Buy when reliability, observability, and predictable unit economics matter."

Buyer personas & primary motivations
- ML Platform Lead: control, custom kernels, model licensing, latency optimization.
- Head of Infrastructure / Cloud Ops: security boundaries (VPC / air-gapped), cost predictability, maintenance overhead.
- Product Engineering Manager: time-to-market, SLAs for customer-facing features.

Common reasons customers pick self-hosted and our counters
- "Lower cost per token." -> Counter: raw GPU-hour cost can be lower, but total cost of ownership (engineering, ops, SRE, incident MTTR, and persistent infra investments) usually erodes that advantage by 30–100% on first-year TCO for teams without a dedicated infra org. Provide a sample TCO: cluster engineering FTEs (2–3), SRE support (0.5–1 FTE), GPU ops, orchestration, and ongoing benchmarking cycles.
- "Control & custom kernels/ops." -> Counter: Redwood supports pinned model versions, quantization profiles, custom kernel guidance with our Optimize toolkit and supports private deployments where customers bring specialized kernels (via our private deployment program) with much less operational burden.
- "Data residency / compliance." -> Counter: Redwood Private offers VPC/on-prem packaging + KMS/HSM integrations and audit logs; highlight recent SOC/ISO artifacts and the Private deployment success stories.
- "We already have prototypes on vLLM/TGI." -> Counter: prototypes rarely account for production workload patterns (burstiness, KV cache, long-running contexts). Redwood’s smart routing, automatic KV/prefix caching, and canary rollouts mitigate production surprises.

Tech comparison (concise heuristic table, for quick SE reference)
- vLLM/TGI (OSS stacks): + Rapid iteration, free software, strong community; - You own orchestration, CV/driver updates, memory/cliff edge tuning, and debugging; variable performance by model/token lengths.
- TensorRT-LLM & proprietary kernels: + Best raw latency per GPU for supported models; - Fragile across model versions, limited model compatibility, heavier engineering integration.
- Managed Redwood (hosted/dedicated/private): + SLA, telemetry, cost controls (batching/kv/cache/quantization guidance), rollout tooling; - Less raw control of kernel internals (we partner for kernel specialists when required).

Operational risk & hidden costs (talking points)
- Incident remediation: who owns MTTR for a bad model update or memory leak? Teams often under-budget for oncall and paging fatigue.
- Performance regressions during model upgrades: OSS stacks require bespoke perf testing, often skipped. Redwood’s Evaluate & Optimize workflows guard against regressions with prompt-based evals.
- Capacity planning & peak bursts: self-hosted often needs large headroom. Redwood’s dedicated pool and autoscaling policies reduce committed capacity while preserving SLOs.

Realistic cost heuristics to use in field (very high level)
- Example (conservative): self-hosted P99 latency-suitable cluster for high-throughput chat: 4–8 A100-class GPUs + 1 infra engineer + 0.5 SRE = heavy fixed base. First-year all-in costs often approach or exceed Redwood Dedicated + engineering uplift for many mid-market customers.
- Use our internal calculator link (CONFLUENCE-1234) to run client numbers, always show both per-token and per-month committed cost lines.

POC recipe (recommended path to win)
1) Discovery call (1 hour): quantify throughput, concurrency, latency targets, compliance constraints, and uptime needs.
2) Fast baseline: Redwood hosted run of a production-ish prompt set (1–3 days) to demonstrate latency/cost and quality parity.
3) Optional Private POC: run in the customer VPC with a fixed dataset/traffic replay (2–4 weeks) to validate PKI/KMS, and network egress policies.
4) Success metrics: sustained p99 latency target met, consistent generation quality (no regressions vs baseline), cost per active user within threshold, incidentless 2-week run.
5) Next steps: transition plan to Dedicated or Private; handoff docs for SRE/Platform.

Sales plays and collateral to prioritize
- "Time-to-Production Play": emphasize weeks-to-prod vs months, include sample runbook and rollout checklist.
- "SLA & Compliance Play": target regulated industries with Private deployment + Audit package.
- "Ops Cost Avoidance Play": show FTE savings and MTTR reduction metrics from existing customer case studies.

Objection handling snippets (short)
- Objection: "We can tune vLLM to reduce token cost by X%." Response: "Great — we can run the same tuning on Dedicated/Private with you. Our Optimize toolkit codifies those knobs and we can pair on kernel/quant profiles during a POC so you get the benefit without the ops debt."
- Objection: "We need on-prem because cloud is blocked." Response: "We have an air-gapped on-prem pattern and a Private control plane option; recommend a hybrid POC to prove parity first."

Message framing for marketing assets (one-liners)
- "Ship production-grade inference without building an inference ops team."
- "Control when you must, outsource the rest: predictable SLAs + custom private deployments."

Open questions / unknowns to validate with eng/product
- How to position when buyer's primary metric is pure $/token for huge steady-state high-volume (we need more benchmark-ed examples).
- What preapproved kernel partners can we name in sales decks for customers demanding kernel-level tuning?
- Clarify lead-time and cost estimate for fully air-gapped on-prem packaging (legal/ops costs beyond infra).

Action items (short)
- SEs: capture 3 customer POCs where self-hosted was chosen then re-evaluated within 12 months; extract failure modes. (Owner: Miguel)
- Product: prepare two one-page artifacts: "Private deployment checklist" and "Optimize: quantization & batching guide". (Owner: Hannah)
- GTM: update handoff bundle with POC playbook and pricing calculator link. (Owner: Ethan)

Slack refs / useful links
- #g2m-inference-sales for POC signals, paste winning objection examples.
- CONFLUENCE-1234: internal cost calculator (benchmark inputs).

Notes to self
- Keep this doc lean — field teams prefer bullets and scripts. We should create a detachable 1-page cheat sheet for AE/SEs and a 2-slide "Build vs Buy" visual for decks.
- Revisit after next three customer POCs to add quantitative TCO examples.
